cards.anchor: N1 is recognized yet dashboard-pending through boundary 3; registration and recognition are independently measurable.
cards.burden: The registration clerk performs six validations. The dispatcher performs six request actions and maintains the identity-selection plan against recognition and queue ledgers at boundaries. Ledger reads add no modeled clerk labor; plan adherence and checking remain dispatcher responsibilities.
cards.construction: Validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0 through 5. Request individual N2,N3,N4 at ticks 0,1,2; bulk at 4 for N5,N6; individual N7 at 5 and N8 at 6. The existing FIFO server delivers.
cards.defeat: Carrier dependency attack: replace only the tick-0 individual request with bulk while keeping the remaining candidate actions. This feasible six-action variant predicts seven recognitions: duplicate N1 delays N4 until tick 4, so bulk at 4 also duplicates N4 and N8 misses the window. Candidate success is defeated by fewer than eight registrations or recognitions, or excess actions.
cards.mutation: Move acknowledgment identity selection from the bulk pending display into a dispatcher arrangement using the recognition ledger and timed request plan. Its dependency is correct reconciliation and execution; it adds no delivery capacity.
cards.prediction_candidate: Derived finite-model prediction: eight registrations and eight recognitions by boundary 9, including initial N1. First deliveries are N2 at 1, N3 at 2, N4 at 3, N5 at 5, N6 at 6, N7 at 7, N8 at 8; six actions.
cards.prediction_rival: Derived prediction: eight registrations but only three recognitions, N1,N2,N3, by boundary 9. Early duplicate entries occupy FIFO delivery ticks; six actions are spent.
cards.probe: Replay candidate and rival with identical validation order and request ticks, then replay the carrier attack. Compare registration, recognition, request, queue and dashboard ledgers at every boundary. These are schedule predictions, not observed trials.
cards.rival: Use routine bulk at every candidate request tick: 0,1,2,4,5,6.
unknowns: N1 delay origin is unknown; no wider defect follows.
Later sender adaptation and additional demand are unobserved hypotheses.
No empirical network comparison or globally best schedule proof is supplied.
